claim: The Reliability Pillar (REL06-BP01) recommends monitoring the components of the workload with Amazon CloudWatch or third-party tools and monitoring AWS services with the AWS Health Dashboard, covering the front-end, business logic and storage tiers.
question: What does the Reliability Pillar recommend for monitoring a workload?

values.display: with Amazon CloudWatch or third-party tools
Monitor AWS services with AWS Health Dashboard
front-end, business logic, and storage tiers

evidence.quote: Monitor the components of the workload with Amazon CloudWatch or third-party tools. Monitor AWS services with AWS Health Dashboard.
All components of your workload should be monitored, including the front-end, business logic, and storage tiers.

claim: The Reliability Pillar says a metric related to business outcomes, such as the number of orders successfully processed per minute, can indicate workload issues faster than a technical metric such as CPU utilization.
question: Which metrics should drive the alarms of a highly available workload?

values.display: a metric related to business outcomes
can indicate workload issues faster than technical metric

evidence.quote: For example, a metric related to business outcomes such as the number of orders successfully processed per minute, can indicate workload issues faster than technical metric, such as CPU Utilization.

claim: The Reliability Pillar recommends monitoring all external endpoints so that they are independent of your base implementation, with synthetic transactions (user canaries); Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics lets you create synthetic canaries to monitor your endpoints and APIs.
question: How do you monitor the availability of your endpoints from the user's point of view?

values.display: monitor all of your external endpoints
CloudWatch Synthetics allows you to create synthetic canaries

evidence.quote: In addition, monitor all of your external endpoints to ensure that they are independent of your base implementation.

Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics allows you to [create synthetic canaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries.html) to monitor your endpoints and APIs.

claim: The Reliability Pillar (REL06-BP03) recommends real-time processing and alarming to improve the detectability of issues that could affect availability, and to serve as triggers for automated response.
question: Why does the Reliability Pillar recommend alarms on workload metrics?

values.display: improve the detectability of issues
serve as triggers for automated response

evidence.quote: Workloads should be equipped with real-time processing and alarming to improve the detectability of issues that could impact the availability of the application and serve as triggers for automated response.

claim: The Reliability Pillar (REL06-BP04) says automated responses to alarms could include replacing failing components, adjusting compute capacity, redirecting traffic to healthy hosts, Availability Zones or other Regions, and notifying operators.
question: What automated responses to alarms does the Reliability Pillar list?

values.display: replacement of failing components
adjustment of compute capacity

evidence.quote: Automated responses to alarms could include the replacement of failing components, the adjustment of compute capacity, the redirection of traffic to healthy hosts, availability zones, or other regions, and the notification of operators.

claim: The Reliability Pillar (REL06-BP07) recommends tracing requests as they pass through service components so teams can analyze and debug issues more easily, and says you can use AWS X-Ray and CloudWatch Application Monitoring to get a complete view of requests as they travel through your application.
question: Which AWS services give end-to-end tracing of requests according to the Reliability Pillar?

values.display: Trace requests as they process through service components
AWS X-Ray and Amazon CloudWatch Application Monitoring

evidence.quote: Trace requests as they process through service components so product teams can more easily analyze and debug issues and improve performance.

You can use [AWS X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html) and [Amazon CloudWatch Application Monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Application-Monitoring-Sections.html) instrumentation services to provide a complete view of requests as they travel through your application.

claim: The Operational Excellence Pillar (OPS04-BP01) says implementing observability starts with understanding the workload's state and making data-driven decisions based on business requirements, and that defining and monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs) aligns monitoring with business objectives.
question: How does the Operational Excellence Pillar tie monitoring to business needs?

values.display: defining and monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs)
starts with understanding its state

evidence.quote: Implementing observability in your workload starts with understanding its state and making data-driven decisions based on business requirements. One of the most effective ways to ensure alignment between monitoring activities and business objectives is by defining and monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs).

claim: The Operational Excellence Pillar (OPS08-BP04) says basing alerts on KPIs ensures that the signals you receive are directly tied to business or operational impact, and lists too many non-critical alerts, which cause alert fatigue, as an anti-pattern.
question: What makes an alert actionable according to the Operational Excellence Pillar?

values.display: Basing alerts on KPIs
alert fatigue

evidence.quote: Basing alerts on KPIs ensures that the signals you receive are directly tied to business or operational impact.
Setting up too many non-critical alerts, leading to alert fatigue.

claim: The Operational Excellence Pillar (OPS04-BP05) says distributed tracing lets you monitor and visualize requests as they traverse the components of a distributed system, so teams can understand how requests flow and where bottlenecks exist.
question: What does distributed tracing show according to the Operational Excellence Pillar?

values.display: monitor and visualize requests as they traverse
where bottlenecks exist

evidence.quote: Distributed tracing offers a way to monitor and visualize requests as they traverse through various components of a distributed system.
By capturing trace data from multiple sources and analyzing it in a unified view, teams can better understand how requests flow, where bottlenecks exist, and where optimization efforts should focus.

claim: The Security Pillar (SEC04-BP01) says to establish a trail for each AWS account using AWS CloudTrail or an AWS Organizations trail, and to configure an Amazon S3 bucket for it.
question: What does the Security Pillar recommend for CloudTrail logging?

values.display: Establish a trail for each AWS account
an AWS Organizations trail

evidence.quote: Establish a trail for each AWS account using AWS CloudTrail or an AWS Organizations trail, and configure an Amazon S3 bucket for it.

claim: The Security Pillar says CloudTrail is turned on by default with a 90-day retention of management events that can be retrieved through Event history, and for longer retention and visibility of data events you create a trail associated with an S3 bucket and optionally a CloudWatch log group.
question: How do you get longer than 90 days of CloudTrail history according to the Security Pillar?

values.display: turned on by default with a 90-day retention
For longer retention and visibility of data events

evidence.quote: It’s turned on by default with a 90-day retention of management events that can be [retrieved through CloudTrail Event history](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/view-cloudtrail-events.html) using the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or an AWS SDK.

For longer retention and visibility of data events, [create a CloudTrail trail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-create-and-update-a-trail.html) and associate it with an Amazon S3 bucket, and optionally with a Amazon CloudWatch log group.

claim: The Security Pillar recommends Amazon S3 for long retention periods because of its cost effectiveness and flexible lifecycle capabilities, and suggests archiving less frequently accessed logs from CloudWatch Logs to Amazon S3.
question: Where should logs with long retention periods be stored according to the Security Pillar?

values.display: use Amazon S3 for its cost effectiveness
archiving less frequently accessed logs to Amazon S3

evidence.quote: For long retention periods, it is recommended to use Amazon S3 for its cost effectiveness and flexible lifecycle capabilities. If the primary logging option is Amazon CloudWatch Logs, as an option, you should consider archiving less frequently accessed logs to Amazon S3.

claim: The Security Pillar (SEC04-BP02) recommends aggregating security log data into a Log Archive account, a separate AWS account with proper cross-account permissions, which helps prevent log tampering within compromised workloads and environments and gives a single integration point for additional tools.
question: Why store security logs in a separate Log Archive account?

values.display: into a Log Archive account
prevent log tampering within compromised workloads

evidence.quote: To overcome these challenges, consider aggregating all relevant sources of security log data into a Log Archive account as described in [Organizing Your AWS Environment Using Multiple Accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/organizing-your-aws-environment/security-ou-and-accounts.html#log-archive-account).

This practice helps prevent log tampering within compromised workloads and environments, provides a single integration point for additional tools, and offers a more simplified model for configuring data retention and lifecycle.

claim: AWS recommends deploying security analytics tools into a Security Tooling account that is separate from the Log Archive account, which protects the integrity and availability of the logs and log management process, distinct from the tools that access them.
question: Which account should run security analytics tools that read the central logs?

values.display: Security Tooling account
separate from your Log Archive account

evidence.quote: AWS recommends you deploy tools for security analytics that operate in an AWS environment into a [Security Tooling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/organizing-your-aws-environment/security-ou-and-accounts.html#security-tooling-accounts) account that is separate from your Log Archive account. This approach allows you to implement controls at depth to protect the integrity and availability of the logs and log management process, distinct from the tools that access them.

question: Where does AWS list recommended alarms for each service?

values.display: we recommend that you set best practice alarms
recommended threshold, threshold justification

evidence.quote: The following sections list the metrics that we recommend that you set best practice alarms for. For each metric, the dimensions, alarm intent, recommended threshold, threshold justification, and the period length and number of datapoints is also displayed.
